sprint.name: tooling-v0.4
sprint.summary: Fix the operational wrapper that prevents Pidgin from surviving interrupts and persisting partial results at scale (incremental writes, graceful shutdown, progress tracking), consolidate to a single API provider (OpenAI), integrate Pidgin into agent workflows (agent file rewrite, skills rewrite), clean up three sprints of accumulated debt (project restructuring, carry-forward fixes, documentation audits), and attempt a first fine-tune on converged MLD training data. 18 missions across 5 phases. Phase 5 (M16-M18) conditional on M6 producing 500+ converged examples. Expected duration: 2-3 sprint days.

decision_points.dp: Gate model fallback. If gpt-4.1-mini fails G1-G5 probes in M5, the fallback is gpt-5.4-mini. If both fail, gate calls stay on claude-haiku-4-5 and the Anthropic API dependency remains for v0.4. M8 (agent file rewrite) blocks on M5's resolution.

Incremental write granularity. M1 can write per-batch (~20 functions at a time) or accumulate a write queue and flush periodically. Default: per-batch (simpler, matches the existing batch boundary). Commander confirms.

Identity key migration. M14 changes the identity key from absolute path to relative path. Existing nests will see all functions as "new" on next index. Accepted — M6 re-indexes the primary target anyway, and incremental writes (M1) make re-indexing cheap.
Fine-tuning go/no-go. M17 only dispatches if M16 reports 500+ valid examples and recommends go. If M6 produces fewer than 500 converged examples, Phase 5 reduces to M16 + M18 only.
Architecture.md deferral threshold. M15 drops if the sprint exceeds its time budget. Commander decides the threshold at runtime.

mission.context:
The pipeline currently collects all results in memory and writes the nest only at the end of the run. Two failed runs on the OpenAI Python SDK (4930 functions) demonstrated the problem: Run 1 ran 40 minutes, processed ~300 functions, then the operator Ctrl+C'd to move terminals — all results lost. Run 2 restarted, idempotency showed 0 unchanged / 4930 new because nothing persisted.
The pipeline is all-or-nothing. A 27-hour job that fails at hour 26 loses everything.
Key code locations: - pidgin/pipeline/batch.py: run_embedding_mld_pipeline_for_functions() orchestrates the full generate + embed pipeline. The batch path builds all GenerationRequests upfront (line ~1017), submits via run_batch_generation (line ~1028), then builds EmbeddingRequests for all candidates (line ~1057), embeds (line ~1067), and constructs FunctionMldResult objects (line ~1088). All results are returned as a single list to the caller. - pidgin/verbs/index.py: run() receives the full results list (line ~269), then calls upsert_function_descriptions() once with all results (line ~384). - pidgin/store/nest.py: upsert_function_descriptions() iterates the results list and upserts each to ChromaDB (line ~849). - pidgin/store/sft.py: append() writes SFT records to training-data.jsonl. Currently called once after all MLD completes (index.py line ~362).
PD2: per-batch upsert (simpler, matches existing batch boundary).
mission.objective: 1. After each batch chunk completes (~100 requests, ~20 functions), upsert converged results into the per-repo ChromaDB nest immediately. 2. Write SFT training data (training-data.jsonl) incrementally — append after each batch, not bulk-write at end. 3. Generate file-level summaries per-file as that file's functions complete, not in a bulk pass at the end. 4. Verify: index 50 functions, Ctrl+C after batch 2 (~40 functions), verify nest contains results from completed batches. Restart same command, verify idempotency reports ~40 unchanged and ~10 new.
mission.specification:
The batch path in run_embedding_mld_pipeline_for_functions currently runs all generation, then all embedding, then returns results. M1 restructures the BATCH path to process in chunk-sized increments and write after each.
**Approach: per-chunk processing loop in the batch path.**
The current batch path (lines ~1016-1167 in batch.py) does: 1. Build all GenerationRequests upfront 2. run_batch_generation (all at once) 3. Flatten drafts → candidates per function 4. Build all EmbeddingRequests 5. Embed all 6. Build FunctionMldResults
M1 restructures this so that after each generation chunk completes (via _submit_chunks_pipelined, which already processes chunks sequentially), the pipeline immediately embeds and constructs FunctionMldResult for the functions in that chunk.
**File: pidgin/pipeline/batch.py**
Add a new function:
```python def run_incremental_mld_pipeline( functions: list[dict], *, converge_template: str, max_batches: int, convergence_threshold: float, dispatch: str, verbose: bool, on_chunk_complete: "Callable[[list[FunctionMldResult], list[dict]], None] | None" = None, ) -> list[FunctionMldResult]: ```
This function replaces the batch path inside run_embedding_mld_pipeline_for_functions. It: 1. Builds all GenerationRequests upfront (same as current). 2. Instead of calling run_batch_generation (which merges everything), calls _chunk_requests to split into chunks, then processes each chunk through the pipelined submitter. 3. After each generation chunk completes: a. Flatten drafts for the functions covered by this chunk. b. Build EmbeddingRequests for those candidates. c. Embed them (sync for small batches, batch for large). d. Construct FunctionMldResult objects for the completed functions. e. Call on_chunk_complete(chunk_results, chunk_functions) if provided. 4. Return the full accumulated results list.
The on_chunk_complete callback is how index.py hooks in to upsert and write SFT data after each chunk.
**Mapping chunks to functions:** Each generation chunk contains requests with custom_id format "gen:func={fi}:call={ci}". A chunk of 100 requests with max_batches=5 covers 20 functions (100/5). The pipeline tracks which function indices (fi) are fully complete (all max_batches calls returned) after each chunk. Only fully-complete functions are emitted in on_chunk_complete.
**File: pidgin/verbs/index.py**
Modify run() to pass an on_chunk_complete callback to the pipeline:
```python def _on_chunk(chunk_results, chunk_funcs): # 1. Upsert to nest nest.upsert_function_descriptions( repo_root_abs, chunk_results, chunk_funcs, file_meta=file_meta_by_rel, ) # 2. Append SFT records sft_records = _build_sft_records(chunk_results, chunk_funcs) if sft_records: _sft.append(repo_root_abs, sft_records) # 3. File-level summary for any files now fully complete _maybe_synthesise_summaries(chunk_funcs, chunk_results) ```
Extract the SFT record building logic (currently inline at lines ~318-367) into a helper function _build_sft_records(results, funcs) -> list[SFTRecord].
Extract the file summary logic (currently at lines ~397-455) into a helper _maybe_synthesise_summaries(funcs, results) that checks whether all functions in a given file have been processed before generating the summary. Track completed files in a module-level or closure-scoped set.
**File: pidgin/store/sft.py**
No changes needed — append() already writes incrementally.
**Sync path:** The sync path (_run_pipeline_sync_adaptive) processes one function at a time. M1 adds on_chunk_complete support there too: call the callback after each function completes (chunk size of 1). This ensures Ctrl+C resilience on the sync path as well.

mission.context:
The current KeyboardInterrupt handling in the index verb produces 50+ lines of httpx/asyncio traceback. A `RuntimeError: Event loop is closed` async cleanup error from v0.3 stress tests is cosmetic but alarming. After M1 lands incremental writes, the interrupt handler can rely on partial results already being persisted — it just needs to flush any in-flight data and exit cleanly.
This mission depends on M1: the graceful shutdown path uses M1's incremental write mechanism to ensure whatever results have been collected are already in the nest. The interrupt handler's job is to suppress tracebacks and print a clean summary.
Key code locations: - pidgin/verbs/index.py: run() is the top-level entry point. The KeyboardInterrupt must be caught here. - pidgin/pipeline/batch.py: _submit_chunks_pipelined() has a polling loop (line ~439) that sleeps and polls. KeyboardInterrupt during time.sleep() propagates up.
mission.objective: 1. Catch KeyboardInterrupt at the top level of the index verb. 2. On interrupt: do not wait for in-flight batch polling. Print a clean one-line summary. Exit 130 (standard SIGINT exit code). 3. Suppress the RuntimeError: Event loop is closed async cleanup error. 4. After M2, Ctrl+C during an index run produces exactly one summary line and no traceback.
mission.specification:
**File: pidgin/verbs/index.py**
Wrap the live-mode body of run() (everything after the dry-run early return, from the imports at line ~164 through the return 0 at line ~459) in a try/except KeyboardInterrupt block:
```python try: # ... existing live-mode body ... except KeyboardInterrupt: # M1's incremental writes mean partial results are already persisted. # Count what we have. n_written = _chunk_write_count # closure variable from the callback n_total = len(to_mld) if 'to_mld' in dir() else len(funcs) print( f"\nInterrupted. Wrote {n_written}/{n_total} functions to nest. " f"Resume with the same command to continue.", file=sys.stderr, ) sys.exit(130) ```
The _chunk_write_count variable is incremented by the on_chunk_complete callback from M1. If the interrupt happens before any chunks complete, it will be 0.
**Suppress async cleanup errors:**
At the module level of index.py (or in the except block), add:
```python import warnings warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", message=".*Event loop is closed.*") ```
Alternatively, catch RuntimeError in a top-level atexit handler that checks for "Event loop is closed" in the message. The simpler approach (warnings filter) is preferred — it's one line and catches the specific cosmetic error without masking real RuntimeErrors.
**File: pidgin/pipeline/batch.py**
In _submit_chunks_pipelined, the time.sleep(poll_interval_s) at line ~440 is where KeyboardInterrupt most commonly fires during polling. No change needed here — let the exception propagate to the index verb's handler. Do NOT add a local try/except in batch.py — that would mask the interrupt from the verb layer.
**Test (manual, documented in report):** 1. Start `pidgin index <path> --batch` on a directory with 50+ functions. 2. Ctrl+C during batch polling. 3. Observe: one summary line, no traceback, exit code 130. 4. Restart same command. Verify resume (idempotency from M1).

mission.context:
The AST parser (pidgin/utils/parser.py) only extracts module-level `def` statements and top-level class definitions. Three OpenAI SDK subdirectories (embeddings, files, batches) returned zero functions because they are class-based — public methods are inside class bodies but the parser's _python_record() (line ~189) walks ast.walk(tree), which visits all nodes including class methods, but parse_python() does not distinguish class methods from module-level defs. The actual problem is that _python_record skips private names (starting with _) and extracts both top-level and nested functions — but class methods appear with their bare names (e.g. "create"), not qualified (e.g. "Embeddings.create"). This means: 1. Class methods DO get extracted, but their name collides with methods from other classes. 2. The module field degrades to basename (e.g. "parser.py" instead of "pidgin/utils/parser.py") when called on individual files.
M4 fixes: (a) class method identity uses ClassName.method_name, (b) module field uses relative path from repo root, (c) single-file indexing works via walk_source_files.
Key code locations: - pidgin/utils/parser.py: parse_python() at line ~171, _python_record() at line ~189, extract_public_functions() at line ~554, walk_source_files() at line ~39.

Verify single-file indexing works via walk_source_files.
mission.specification:
**File: pidgin/utils/parser.py**
**Change 1: Class method extraction in parse_python (line ~171)**
Replace the current ast.walk approach with a two-pass extraction:
```python def parse_python(source: str, module_path: str) -> list[FunctionRecord]: try: tree = ast.parse(source) except SyntaxError: return []
lines = source.splitlines() records: list[FunctionRecord] = []
for node in ast.iter_child_nodes(tree): # Module-level functions if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)): rec = _python_record(node, lines, module_path, class_name=None) if rec is not None: records.append(rec) # Classes: extract public methods elif isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef): # Add a record for the class itself class_rec = _python_record(node, lines, module_path, class_name=None) if class_rec is not None: records.append(class_rec) # Extract methods for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node): if isinstance(child, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)): method_rec = _python_record( child, lines, module_path, class_name=node.name, ) if method_rec is not None: records.append(method_rec)
return records ```
**Change 2: Update _python_record to accept class_name (line ~189)**
```python def _python_record( node, lines: list[str], module_path: str, class_name: str | None = None, ) -> "FunctionRecord | None": if not isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)): return None
name = node.name
# For class methods: qualify with ClassName.method_name if class_name is not None: # Skip private methods (leading _) except __init__ if name.startswith("_") and name != "__init__": return None # Skip __dunder__ methods except __init__ if name.startswith("__") and name.endswith("__") and name != "__init__": return None # __init__: only keep if body has meaningful logic beyond assignment if name == "__init__": if not _init_has_meaningful_logic(node): return None name = f"{class_name}.{name}" else: # Module-level: skip private names as before if name.startswith("_") and name != "__init__": return None
# ... rest unchanged (start, end, signature, body, visibility, return) ```
**Change 3: Add __init__ logic checker**
```python def _init_has_meaningful_logic(node) -> bool: """Return True if __init__ body contains logic beyond self.x = x assignments.
Checks for: function calls (not super().__init__), control flow (if/for/while/try), list comprehensions, or any statement that is not a simple assignment. """ for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node): if isinstance(child, (ast.If, ast.For, ast.While, ast.Try, ast.With)): return True if isinstance(child, ast.Expr) and isinstance(child.value, ast.Call): # Allow super().__init__() but flag other calls func = child.value.func if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(func.value, ast.Call): continue # super().__init__() return True return False ```
**Change 4: Fix module field in extract_public_functions (line ~554)**
The current code at line ~592 computes module_path relative to the file's parent (for single files) or root (for directories). The problem is single-file mode uses file_path.parent, which gives just the basename.
Fix: always compute module_path relative to the repo root (found via find_project_root), falling back to the current behaviour if no git root exists.
```python from pidgin.utils.git import find_project_root
# In extract_public_functions, replace the module_path computation: repo_root = find_project_root(str(root)) if repo_root: repo_root_p = Path(repo_root) else: repo_root_p = root.parent if root.is_file() else root
for file_path in sorted(candidates): # ... try: module_path = str(file_path.relative_to(repo_root_p)) except ValueError: module_path = str(file_path) ```
**Change 5: walk_source_files single-file handling**
walk_source_files already handles single files (CF4 guard at line ~60). Verify it works and document in the report. No code change expected.
